verses.text: Some time later, David defeated the Philistines and brought them under his control. He took Gath and its villages from the Philistines.
He also defeated Moab, and the Moabites became David's servants and paid him taxes.
David also defeated Hadadezer king of Zobah, near Hamath, when Hadadezer went to set up his control along the Euphrates River.
David captured from him a thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. He crippled all the chariot horses except enough for a hundred chariots.
When the Syrians from Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David killed twenty-two thousand of them.
Then David put groups of soldiers in the Syrian kingdom of Damascus, and the Syrians became David's servants and paid him taxes. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
David took the gold shields that Hadadezer's officers carried and brought them to Jerusalem.

From Tibhath and Cun, towns that belonged to Hadadezer, David took a great amount of bronze. Later Solomon used it to make the huge bronze tank called the Sea, the pillars, and the bronze objects for the temple.
Tou king of Hamath heard that David had defeated the whole army of Hadadezer king of Zobah.

So he sent his son Hadoram to King David to greet him and congratulate him on his victory over Hadadezer, because Tou had often been at war with Hadadezer. Hadoram brought all kinds of objects made of gold, silver, and bronze.
King David gave these to the LORD, along with the silver and gold he had taken from all the nations: from Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, and Amalek.
Abishai son of Zeruiah killed eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
He put groups of soldiers in Edom, and all the Edomites became David's servants. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
David ruled over all Israel. He did what was fair and right for all his people.
Joab son of Zeruiah was in charge of the army. Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the record keeper.
Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar were priests. Shavsha was the secretary.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was in charge of the Cherethites and Pelethites, the king's bodyguard. David's sons were the chief officials at the king's side.
